## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Mahantaraduka* (Patthana 2.10) is a section of the *Paṭṭhāna*, the seventh and concluding text of the Abhidhamma Piṭaka in the Pali Canon [SuttaCentral]. In the architecture of the Theravāda Abhidhamma, the *mahantaraduka* constitutes the "longer intermediate set of fourteen dyads" within the Abhidhamma matrix (*mātikā*), addressing miscellaneous pairs of conditional factors, many of which specifically analyze the mutual relations between awareness (*citta*) and mental states (*cetasika*) [Potter 1996]. Within the *Paṭṭhāna*, this section subjects these fourteen dyads to the comprehensive system of twenty-four conditional relations (*paccaya*).
SuttaCentral does not list any curated parallels for this section [SuttaCentral]. However, the DharmaNexus text-reuse algorithm aligns segments of the *Mahantaraduka* with several Northern Buddhist Abhidharma and Yogācāra texts [DharmaNexus]. The closest match occurs with Ghoṣaka's Sanskrit *Abhidharmāmṛta* (e.g., §292.0.2–292.0.4 matching §935–936 with a score of 85) [DharmaNexus]. Other cross-language alignments include the Tibetan translation of the *Abhidharmakośabhāṣyaṭīkā Tattvārtha* (D4421), Vasubandhu's *Abhidharmakośabhāṣya* (D4090 and Sanskrit Chapter 1), Asaṅga's *Abhidharmasamuccaya*, Sthiramati's *Pañcaskandhakavibhāṣā*, the *Pratītyasamutpādādivibhaṅganirdeśaṭīkā* (D3996), the *Saṃskṛtāsaṃskṛtaviniścaya* (D3897), Harivarman's *Tattvasiddhiśāstra* (*Satyasiddhiśāstra*), and the *Yogācārabhūmi* and *Śrāvakabhūmi* [DharmaNexus]. These machine alignments reflect shared Abhidharmic terminology and definitions rather than direct textual lineage.
Direct secondary scholarship on this specific *Paṭṭhāna* chapter is minimal, as modern scholarship on the *mahantaraduka* dyads primarily discusses their enumeration in the *Dhammasaṅgaṇi*, their treatment in the *Dhātukathā*, and their broader structural position within the Abhidhamma *mātikā*.
